#Main Hypotheses

1) Consistent with previous research on behavioral economics and moral decision making, we hypothesize that participants will be more psychologically risk averse to harm than gain motivated.

2) Participants risk aversion to harm will change as the cognitive domain being treated changes. Specifically, participants will be more risk averse to mood, and self-control because these are more central to self-identity.

3) Participants who are more affluent, educated, liberal, and younger will be risk seeking relative to the average risky decision making behavior observed when judging treatments for others.

library(tidyverse)
library(psych)
library(car)
library(mfx)

```{r Import and Transform task data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Disable scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

#note to pull data in terminal: aws s3 sync s3://neuroethics-task .
files <- list.files(path = "../data/mturk_data/mturk_data_05202020", pattern = "*.csv", full.names = T)

#combine all the task csv into a list

pilot <- sapply(files, readr::read_csv, simplify=FALSE) 
raw.data = bind_rows(pilot)

#get needed variables from from pulled csv for each subject
raw.data %>% 
 dplyr::select(user_id, condition, total_trials, risk, gain ,no_effect, experimental_treatment_selected, key_press, rt) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  filter(total_trials >= 75) %>% 
  mutate(ratio = gain / risk) -> clean.data #Gain over Risk

clean.data$condition = factor(clean.data$condition) 
clean.data$experimental_treatment_selected = as.integer(clean.data$experimental_treatment_selected)

clean.data$experimental_treatment_selected = factor(clean.data$experimental_treatment_selected, labels = c("No to treatment","Yes to treatment"))
```

```{r get betas for within subject models}
clean.data %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id,risk,gain,ratio, rt, experimental_treatment_selected) %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>% 
  #mutate(risk = -risk) %>% 
  mutate(risk.c = scale(risk, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(gain.c = scale(gain, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) -> logit.data 

m.logit <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) glm(treatment ~ 1  + risk.c + gain.c, data = x, family = binomial(link = "logit"),control=glm.control(maxit=50)))

#Compute beta
user_id <- names(m.logit)
n = nrow(logit.data)/75
n=456
betas <- list()
colin <- list()

for (i in 1:n){
dat = m.logit[[i]]$coefficients
  betas[[i]] = dat
}

subjectModels <- do.call(rbind, betas)
colnames(subjectModels) <-  c('Intercept', 'Risk_Beta', 'Gain_Beta') #interaction removed
subjectModels <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels)

#check the variance inflation factors 
for (i in user_id){
vif <- car::vif(m.logit[[i]])
colin[[i]] <- vif
}

subjectcolin <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, colin))
subjectcolin <- tibble::rownames_to_column(subjectcolin, "user_id")
colnames(subjectcolin) <-  c("user_id","vif.risk", "vif.gain")

#loop the r^2 calculator on the fitted final model
subject.r2 = list() 

for (i in 1:n){
  LogModel <- m.logit[[i]]
  dev <- LogModel$deviance 
  nullDev <- LogModel$null.deviance 
  modelN <-  length(LogModel$fitted.values)
  R.cs <- 1- exp ( -(nullDev - dev) / modelN)
  dat <- R.cs / ( 1 - ( exp (-(nullDev / modelN))))
  subject.r2[[i]] = dat
}


subjectModels.r2 <- do.call(rbind, subject.r2)
colnames(subjectModels.r2) <-  c("Nagelkerke_R2")

subjectModels.r2 <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels.r2)
 
subjectModels.r2 %>%    
   filter(!Nagelkerke_R2 == -Inf) %>% 
   filter(!Nagelkerke_R2 <= quantile(subjectModels.r2$Nagelkerke_R2, .05)) -> index


clean.data <-  merge(clean.data, index, "user_id")

#remove subject if they have vif for risk or gain above 4 
subjectcolin %>% 
  filter(!vif.risk > 5) %>% 
  filter(!vif.gain > 5) -> index 

#merge the subject models extracted above and the index
subjectModels <- merge(subjectModels, index, "user_id")

clean.data <-  merge(clean.data, subjectModels, "user_id")

#calculate average marginal effects
m.marginal <-  by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) logitmfx(treatment ~ risk.c + gain.c, control=glm.control(maxit=50), data = x))

user_id <- names(m.marginal)
marginal.effect <- list()
n = 456
for (i in 1:n){
dat = m.marginal[[i]]$mfxest[c(1,2,7,8)]
  marginal.effect[[i]] = dat
}
subjectModels.marginal <- do.call(rbind, marginal.effect)
colnames(subjectModels.marginal) <-  c("marginal.effect.risk", "marginal.effect.gain", "marginal.effect.P.risk","marginal.effect.P.gain")

subjectModels.marginal <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels.marginal)  

clean.data <-  merge(clean.data, subjectModels.marginal, "user_id")
```

```{r Pseduo R^2s, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
#loop the r^2 calculator on the fitted final model
subject.r2 = list() 

for (i in 1:n){
  LogModel <- m.logit[[i]]
  dev <- LogModel$deviance 
  nullDev <- LogModel$null.deviance 
  modelN <-  length(LogModel$fitted.values)
  R.cs <- 1- exp ( -(nullDev - dev) / modelN)
  dat <- R.cs / ( 1 - ( exp (-(nullDev / modelN))))
  subject.r2[[i]] = dat
}


subjectModels.r2 <- do.call(rbind, subject.r2)
colnames(subjectModels.r2) <-  c("Nagelkerke_R2")

subjectModels.r2 <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels.r2)
 
subjectModels.r2 %>% 
   filter(!Nagelkerke_R2 == -Inf) %>% 
   filter(!Nagelkerke_R2 <= quantile(subjectModels.r2$Nagelkerke_R2, .05)) -> index


clean.data <-  merge(clean.data, index, "user_id")
```

```{r p values, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
datalist.pvalue = list()
for (i in user_id){
dat = coef(summary(m.logit[[i]]))[,4]#This is coef pvalues
  datalist.pvalue[[i]] = dat
}
subjectModel.Pvalue <-bind_rows(datalist.pvalue)

colnames(subjectModel.Pvalue) <-  c('Intercept_sig','Risk_sig', 'Gain_sig')#removed interaction

for (ii in 1:3){
  for(jj in 1:n){
    if (subjectModel.Pvalue[jj,ii] > 0.05)
    subjectModel.Pvalue[jj,ii] <- 0
    else 
      subjectModel.Pvalue[jj,ii] <- 1
  }
}
subjectModel.Pvalue <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModel.Pvalue)
subjectModel.Pvalue$Risk_sig <-  factor(subjectModel.Pvalue$Risk_sig, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Not Significant","Significant"))
subjectModel.Pvalue$Gain_sig <-  factor(subjectModel.Pvalue$Gain_sig, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Not Significant","Significant"))
#subjectModel.Pvalue$Interaction_sig <-  factor(subjectModel.Pvalue$Interaction_sig, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Not Significant","Significant"))

subjectModels <- cbind.data.frame(subjectModels, subjectModel.Pvalue[,c("Risk_sig", "Gain_sig")])
```

```{r self report data quality check, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
Self.Report <- cbind(survey[,"user_id"], survey[,189:195])

colnames(Self.Report) <- c('user_id',
                           'accurate',
                           'without.reading',
                           'rushed', 
                           'include.data',
                           'randomly',
                           'effort',
                           'careful.thought')

Remove.1 <- Self.Report %>% #Remove by self reported randomness apprasial
  filter(randomly >=5)

Remove.2 <- Self.Report %>%  #Remove by self reported subjective data quality 
  filter(!randomly >=5) %>%
  filter(include.data <=3)

Remove.3 <- Self.Report %>%  #Remove by self reported rushing
  filter(!randomly >=5) %>%
  filter(!include.data <=3) %>%
  filter(rushed >=5)

Remove <- rbind(Remove.1,Remove.2,Remove.3)

for (i in Remove$user_id){
survey <- survey %>% 
  filter(!str_detect(user_id, i))
}

rm(Remove.1,Remove.2,Remove.3)

clean.data <- merge(clean.data, survey[1], "user_id")
```

```{r Lombrozo Moral Commitments task}
#need to fix how is scored
MC <- cbind(survey[,133:138], survey[1])

Results = list()
for (i in 1:6){
  totals <- apply(MC[i],1,sum)
  Results[[i]] = totals 
}

TEST = do.call(rbind, Results)
colnames(TEST) = survey[,"user_id"]
rownames(TEST) <- c('Lying','Assasination','Torture','Murder','Stealing','ForcedSterilization')
TEST <-  as.data.frame(t(TEST))
XX <- cbind(user_id = MC[,"user_id"], TEST)

XX$consequentialism.score <- apply(XX[,2:6], 1, mean)
XX$moral.commitment <- rep("Deontological", nrow(XX)) 
XX$moral.commitment[XX$consequentialism.score >.5] = "Consequentialist" 
XX$moral.commitment <- as.factor(XX$moral.commitment)
XX$moral.commitment <- relevel(XX$moral.commitment, "Deontological")

clean.data <-  merge(clean.data, XX, "user_id")
```

```{r Berlin Numeracy Test}
Berlin.Numeracy.Test<- cbind(survey[, 176:179], survey[1])
#Scoring = Based on answers to 1-4 questions following
#Correct answers are as follows: 
#1 = 25; 2 = 30; 3 =20; 4 = 50.
Berlin <- c("Berlin1","Berlin2","Berlin3","Berlin4")
Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin1<- ifelse(Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin1 == 25, 1,0)  
Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin2<- ifelse(Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin2 == 30, 1,0)  
Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin3<- ifelse(Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin3 == 20, 1,0)  
Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin4<- ifelse(Berlin.Numeracy.Test$Berlin4 == 50, 1,0)  

Berlin.Numeracy.Test$BerlinScore <- apply(Berlin.Numeracy.Test[,Berlin], 1, function(X) sum(X))
clean.data <-  merge(clean.data, Berlin.Numeracy.Test, "user_id")
```

  dplyr::select(risk,gain,dydx_risk, dydx_gain) %>%

 reshape2::melt(id = c("dydx", "MER"), variable.name = "type", value.name = "index") -> test #resturcture the data

  ggsave(filename = paste0(i , ".pdf"), path = "../images/MER_plots")

          xticks.by = 10,
          #add = "median", rug = TRUE,
          color = "experimental_treatment_selected", 
          fill ="experimental_treatment_selected", 
          palette = c("#FFC20A", "#0C7BDC"))
          ggpar(p3,xlim = c(0,95)) -> p3

  p5 = ggdensity(sub, 
          x = "no_effect",
          ylab = "Response Density",
          xlab = "Probability of no effect (ambiguity)",
          legend = "none",
          xticks.by = 10,
          #add = "median", rug = TRUE,
          color = "experimental_treatment_selected", 
          fill ="experimental_treatment_selected", 
          palette = c("#FFC20A", "#0C7BDC"))
          ggpar(p5,xlim = c(0,95)) -> p5

##Histograms for risk, gain, and no effect
  p2=gghistogram(sub, 
            x = "risk",
            ylab = "Number of Occurrences",
            xlab = "Probability of Loss (risk)",
            add = "median", rug = TRUE,
            fill = "experimental_treatment_selected",  palette = c("#FFC20A", "#0C7BDC"),
            add_density = TRUE, bins = 30,
            legend = "none",
            xticks.by = 10)
            ggpar(p2,xlim = c(0,95)) -> p2

  p4=gghistogram(sub, 
            x = "gain",
            ylab = "Number of Occurrences",
            xlab = "Probability of Gain (benefit)",
            add = "median", rug = TRUE,
            fill = "experimental_treatment_selected",  palette = c("#FFC20A", "#0C7BDC"),
            add_density = TRUE, bins = 30,
            legend = "none",
            xticks.by = 10)
            ggpar(p4,xlim = c(0,95)) -> p4

  p6=gghistogram(sub, 
            x = "no_effect",
            alpha = .5,
            ylab = "Number of Occurrences",
            xlab = "Probability of no effect (ambiguity)",
            add = "median", rug = TRUE,
            fill = "experimental_treatment_selected",  palette = c("#FFC20A", "#0C7BDC"),
            add_density = TRUE, bins = 30, 
            legend = "none",
            xticks.by = 10)
            ggpar(p6,xlim = c(0,95)) -> p6


  png(filename = paste0(i , ".png"),
    width = 1234, height = 468)
  multiplot(p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, cols=3)
  dev.off()
}
